questions.q: Which statement about triangles is TRUE?
options: The interior angles of an equilateral triangle are equal
All sides of an isosceles triangle are equal
The interior angles of an obtuse triangle are all obtuse
A right triangle has 2 right angles
questions.why: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal angles (60° each). An isosceles triangle has only 2 equal sides.

questions.q: Which statement about triangles is FALSE?
options: The interior angles of an obtuse triangle are all obtuse
An isosceles triangle has 2 equal sides
There is 1 right angle inside a right triangle
The interior angles of an equilateral triangle are equal
questions.why: An obtuse triangle has only ONE obtuse angle. Two obtuse angles would already be more than 180°.

questions.q: ABC is an equilateral triangle. What is ∠BAC?
questions.why: All 3 angles of an equilateral triangle are equal: 180° ÷ 3 = 60°.

questions.q: ABC is an equilateral triangle and BC = 10 cm. How long is AB?
questions.why: All 3 sides of an equilateral triangle are equal, so AB = BC = 10 cm.

questions.q: DEF is an isosceles triangle with DE = DF and ∠EDF = 40°. What is ∠DEF?
questions.why: (180° - 40°) ÷ 2 = 140° ÷ 2 = 70°. The 2 base angles are equal.

questions.q: JKL is a right triangle with ∠JKL = 90° and ∠KJL = 50°. What is ∠JLK?
questions.why: The other 2 angles of a right triangle add up to 90°: 90° - 50° = 40°.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 70°. What is each of the other 2 angles?
questions.why: 180° - 70° = 110°. Share it between 2 equal angles: 110° ÷ 2 = 55°.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 24°. What is each of the other 2 angles?
questions.why: 180° - 24° = 156°. Share it between 2 equal angles: 156° ÷ 2 = 78°.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 110°. What is each of the other 2 angles?
questions.why: 180° - 110° = 70°. Share it between 2 equal angles: 70° ÷ 2 = 35°.

questions.q: ABC is a triangle with ∠ACB = 90° and AC = CB = 5 cm. What type of triangle is it?
questions.why: It has a right angle AND 2 equal sides, so it is right and isosceles.

questions.q: Triangle EFG has EF = EG = 5 cm and GF = 4 cm. What type of triangle is it?
questions.why: 2 sides are equal (5 cm and 5 cm), so it is isosceles.

questions.q: A straight line from the center of a circle to its circumference is called the…
questions.why: The radius goes from the center to the edge.

questions.q: A straight line joining any two points on the circumference is called a…
questions.why: Any line joining 2 points on the edge is a chord. A diameter is the longest chord.

questions.q: To draw circle J with diameter 4 cm, you open your compass to…
questions.why: The compass is set to the radius: 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm.

questions.q: Circles K and O each have radius 3 cm. Their circumferences just touch. How far apart are the centers K and O?
questions.why: From K to the touching point is 3 cm, and from there to O is 3 cm more: 3 + 3 = 6 cm.

questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle.
questions.why: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°: 180° - 70° - 40° = 70°.

questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle.
questions.why: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°: 180° - 30° - 28° = 122°.

questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle.
questions.why: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°: 180° - 62° - 45° = 73°.

questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle.
questions.why: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°: 180° - 32° - 90° = 58°.

questions.q: ACD is an equilateral triangle and BCD is a straight line. Find ∠b.
questions.why: ∠ACD = 60°. Angles on a straight line add up to 180°: 180° - 60° = 120°.

questions.q: ACD is equilateral. ABC is isosceles with AB = AC and ∠CAB = 36°. Find ∠BCD.
JK = JL and MK = ML. ∠KJL = 70° and ∠MLK = 25°. Find ∠JLM.
STW is equilateral. ∠VSW = ∠VSU = ∠UST. SUV is isosceles. Find ∠SUV.
ABC is a right triangle with ∠ABC = 38°. ∠CAD = ½ ∠CAB. Find ∠DAB.
ABC is isosceles with ∠A = 40°. DBC is equilateral. Find ∠ACD.
ABC and AED are straight lines and BE = ED. Find ∠ABE.
A triangle has angles 47°, 53° and 80°. What type of triangle is it?
questions.why: All 3 angles are less than 90°.

questions.q: A triangle has angles 40°, 115° and 25°. What type of triangle is it?
questions.why: 115° is more than 90°, so it is an obtuse triangle.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, CB is the base. What is the vertex angle?
questions.why: The vertex angle is at the corner that is not on the base: A.

questions.q: A square is cut in half along a diagonal. Each half is…
questions.why: Each half has a square's corner (90°) and 2 sides of the square (equal).

questions.q: A rectangle (not a square) is cut in half along a diagonal. Each half is…
questions.why: It keeps a right angle, but its 3 sides are all different.

questions.q: Which triangle is impossible to draw?
options: One with 1 obtuse and 2 acute angles
One with 1 right angle and 2 acute angles
questions.why: 90° + 90° = 180° already, so there is nothing left for the third angle.

questions.q: You draw triangle KLM with ∠KLM = 70° and ∠LMK = 70°. What will ∠MKL measure?
You know all 3 sides of a triangle. Which tool helps you find the third corner?
questions.why: Draw an arc from each end of the first side. The arcs cross at the third corner.

questions.q: OR is the radius of a circle and OR = 14.5 cm. What is the diameter?
questions.why: Diameter = 2 × radius = 2 × 14.5 = 29 cm.

questions.q: CD is the diameter of a circle and CD = 25 cm. What is the radius?
questions.why: Radius = diameter ÷ 2 = 25 ÷ 2 = 12.5 cm.

questions.q: ABCD is a square inside a circle. Its diagonal BD = 30 cm. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.why: The diagonal goes through the center, so it is a diameter: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm.

questions.q: A wheel is 60 cm tall. What is its radius?
questions.why: The height of the wheel is its diameter: 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm.

questions.q: A circle has radius 9.5 cm. What is its diameter?
A square has diagonals of 4 cm. A circle passes through all 4 corners. What is its radius?
questions.why: From the middle to a corner is half a diagonal: 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm.
